source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Public markets are missing the AI demand picture because they lack visibility into private inference clouds and private frontier labs
summary_extended: Baker argues that public market investors are structurally mispricing AI demand because they lack visibility into the rapidly growing private inference cloud ecosystem, which is not captured in any publicly observable data. Specifically, he points to Anthropic, OpenAI, and private open-source inference cloud providers — including Fireworks, Baseten/Base10, Modal, and Together — as significant and fast-growing consumers of AI compute that generate substantial revenue and, in Anthropic's case, likely meaningful free cash flow. The standard bearish argument that semiconductor capex is outpacing hyperscaler free cash flow is therefore misleading, because it omits these private entities as a major demand source for chips. Baker's investment implication is that the market's bearish read on AI ROI and semiconductor demand is wrong, and that the selloff in AI/semis in mid-2026 reflects an information gap rather than a fundamental deterioration. Investors who can account for private inference cloud demand will recognize that chip consumption and AI monetization are healthier than public data suggests, making the selloff a buying opportunity in AI infrastructure equities.
detail: The market's bearish read on AI ROI is structurally incomplete because it cannot see Anthropic, OpenAI, and private open-source inference clouds (Fireworks, Baseten/Base10, Modal/Model Together) which are growing rapidly and generating significant cash flow. Anthropic is 'almost certainly pumping out significant amounts of free cash flow.' This missing data makes the semiconductor cash flow vs. hyperscaler free cash flow divergence chart misleading.
